reasoning: Recent Texas Senate polling from the last 45 days shows Democrat James Talarico holding a very narrow lead over Republican Ken Paxton, with multiple polls in late July and early August ranging from Talarico +2 to +5. The best current estimate from the polling average is roughly R+0.9 overall, but the race itself is essentially even and may currently lean slightly Democratic within the margin of error. Texas’s statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index is R+8.

sources.name: Texas Southern University / YouGov
sources.details: Texas Southern University/YouGov survey of likely Texas voters found Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 45%, a 2-point Democratic lead within the margin of error.

sources.name: Texas Pulse / Texas A&M Bush School / Recon MR
sources.details: Texas Pulse/Recon MR poll found Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 43%, giving Talarico a 4-point lead.

sources.name: Fox News
sources.details: Fox News poll found Talarico leading Paxton 51% to 48%, a 3-point Democratic lead.

sources.name: Texas Public Opinion Research
sources.details: Texas Public Opinion Research poll found Talarico leading Paxton 45% to 40%, a 5-point Democratic lead.

sources.name: Pollsmax Texas Senate polling average
sources.details: Polling average across 23 included Texas Senate polls shows Paxton at 46.2% and Talarico at 45.3%, a slight Republican advantage overall.

sources.name: Cook Political Report PVI
sources.details: Texas’s statewide Cook Partisan Voting Index is R+8.
